XenotypeDef.label: Kitul
XenotypeDef.description: Kitul are the result of early experimentation into xenogenetics. They are athletic and retain superficial animal characteristics, with keen senses and excellent eyesight.\n\nSubjected to generations of discrimination, they've retreated into insular communities on many planets. While some groups have found acceptance on certain glitterworlds, a significant number have made their way into piracy.
XenotypeDef.descriptionShort: Kitul are the result of early experimentation into xenogenetics. They are athletic and retain superficial animal characteristics, with keen senses and excellent eyesight.

XenotypeDef.label: Artemid
XenotypeDef.description: Artemids are a xenotype created to be a greater part of nature than a natural human ever could be. Possessing a tail and acid spitting glands, this xenotype thrives while working with plants and animals. They can freely ingest certain plant-based drugs.\n\nAs they are the result of xenogenetic modification, independent Artemid communities are rare. They have a reputation for being foppish and vain, and a stereotype has emerged that they are second sons of nobility or dissatisfied rich children who sought an escape from their lives.
XenotypeDef.descriptionShort: Artemids are a xenotype created to be a greater part of nature than a natural human ever could be. Possessing a tail and acid spitting glands, this xenotype thrives while working with plants and animals. They can freely ingest certain plant-based drugs.

XenotypeDef.label: Nizhar
XenotypeDef.description: Created to be a peak physical combatant, Nizhar are highly capable in melee combat and grow tired less quickly than most. These abilities come with a great detriment to many of their other skills, and they grow restless when they are unable to kill. Their extreme metabolic needs render them completely sterile and dependent on wake-up.\n\nNizhar are sometimes deployed alongside hussars in combat situations, but they're competent as stiletto killers, front-line berserkers, and anything in-between. Nizhar are banned on many worlds, in particular because there are no outward signs of their genetic modifications.

These abilities come with a great detriment to many of their other skills, and they grow restless when they are unable to kill. Their extreme metabolic needs render them completely sterile and dependent on wake-up.

XenotypeDef.label: Prole
XenotypeDef.description:
Bred to create the ultimate worker drone, proles are easygoing and dependable. They tend to be skilled at many necessary industrial tasks and are genetically immune to certain stimulants. While they are competent at combat, they recover slowly and are somewhat prone to disease and cancers.

Proles are not the result of genuine curiosity in pushing human limits or populating dead worlds. Rather, they were created due to corporate interest in seeking more efficient workers. Several communities have thrived on various planets even long after their corporate masters have abandoned them. Inspection of their genetics reveal sloppy work, leaving Proles with shorter lifespans and weaker immune systems than baseliners. Even so, the average prole does not lament their position in life - perhaps an intentional result from the crafting of their genetics.

Many Proles retain the tradition of being named after the worker designations of their ancestors, though not all remember this practice. Those named traditionally tend to nickname themselves to preserve individuality.
XenotypeDef.descriptionShort: Bred to create the ultimate worker drone, proles are easygoing and dependable. They tend to be skilled at many necessary industrial tasks and are genetically immune to certain stimulants. While they are competent at combat, they recover slowly and are somewhat prone to disease and cancers.

XenotypeDef.label: gwennin
XenotypeDef.description: Friendly, dog-like xenohumans with strong stomachs, the gwennin are commonly found among yttakin settlements. Unlike the yttakin, Gwennin are far more likely to engage in productive diplomacy with other xenotypes. Gwennin are very social and easy to please, though they are somewhat unimaginative.\n\nThough not every yttakin settlement enjoys the presence of gwennin, they are often tolerated due to their ability to act as a bridge between furskinned and non-furskinned societies. Being smaller, meeker, and easier to deal with, the gwennin often find themselves in subservient roles - not that they particularly mind.
XenotypeDef.descriptionShort: Friendly, dog-like xenohumans with strong stomachs, the gwennin are commonly found among yttakin settlements. Unlike the yttakin, Gwennin are far more likely to engage in productive diplomacy with other xenotypes. Gwennin are very social and easy to please, though they are somewhat unimaginative.

XenotypeDef.label: reaper
XenotypeDef.description: Reapers are medical noncombatants engineered to fulfill a specific role - to hold back the tides of death. Designed to keep tending to people even in hopeless situations, reapers make for excellent doctors and are utterly incapable of violence.\n\nReapers' distinctive horn and deathly pale skin were designed to differentiate them from soldiers on the battlefield. They are excellent doctors, and are even able to out fires using foam sprayed from special glands in their necks. This specific xenotype structure originated on the planet of Rogia. Some variants from other worlds have been retromodded to be able to fight on the front lines, or even be identical in appearance to baseliners.
